claims.claim: You need evidence of indefinite leave to remain.
claims.quote: in most cases, you will only need to demonstrate that you hold valid indefinite leave in the UK in order to meet the lawful residence requirement.
claims.note: The guidance says you normally only need to show you hold valid indefinite leave.

claims.claim: You can give evidence of settled status instead.
claims.quote: If you are an EEA national, supplying evidence of your settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme (EUSS) will also normally meet this requirement.
claims.note: The guidance says evidence of EUSS settled status normally meets the requirement.

claims.claim: The evidence of status can be an eVisa.
claims.note: The citizenship sources do not mention eVisas as evidence; eVisas appear only on the linked Returning Resident page, a different service.

claims.claim: You need passports covering the qualifying period.
claims.note: The text refers to documents showing you were in the UK for the required period but does not say these are passports covering the qualifying period.

claims.quote: If you live in the Channel Islands, Isle of Man or a British Overseas Territory, or if you live elsewhere and want to apply by post you can use Form AN .
claims.note: The guidance says Form AN is used for postal applications, while applications should normally be submitted online.
